newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends flat on lack of imports.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends flat on lack of imports.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed barely moved against the dollar on Wednesday, due to a lack of import covering and demand for call money, dealers said.
The rupee closed at its opening level of 58.35 to the dollar, in dull trade, they said.
"There is no commercial demand due to a lack of imports and speculators are out of the market," said a Seylan Bank dealer.
"And since call money rates are high, banks are more interested in generating rupes," he added.
Call money rates closed at 13 percent, after rising to 15 due to a big foreign bank showing a large borrowing position, dealers said.
"The foreign bank which is borrowing rupees, does not want to unwind its own positions at the current low level," said the Seylan Bank dealer.
Dealers expect banks to sell dollars to the Central Bank on Thursday, in a bid to generate rupees.
